correctness.rationale: The complete 64-component tensor was reconstructed from the exact published multiplication, yielding all eleven distinct nonzero coefficient polynomials. Over any field with 2 invertible they reduce to five necessary-and-sufficient field equations. Case division for p=3 versus p≠3 proves all components and their intersections; af+c² is absolutely irreducible by coprime linear-polynomial coefficients. Inclusion–exclusion gives q³+q²−q or 3q³−2q² points. The 4×4 skew Pfaffian proves rank-four counts. Direct cobracket expansion recovers a,c,d,f and leaves e arbitrary. A standalone replay independently reconstructs the coadjoint identity and exhaustively tests all skew matrices over F3,F5,F7 plus an F9 extension-field check. No finite computation is used as an arbitrary-field proof.

value.rationale: The exact first four-dimensional example chosen by the founding mock-Lie Yang–Baxter paper is a motivated natural test case for its new tensor construction. The result completely determines the previously unspecified skew solution geometry, including a dimension-and-component change unique to characteristic three rather than a routine fixed-field substitution. The nondegenerate (symplectic) solution counts and exact coboundary-fiber classification distinguish genuine operator parameters from identical dual structures; the arithmetic formulas and zeta functions express the structural transition across every finite extension. This is a complete, reproducible natural classification not a tiny arbitrary numerical gain.
